item.wildroots.field_journal.desc: A naturalist's notes. Use to open.
wildroots.message.journal.received: You now carry a field journal.
wildroots.journal.hint.welcome.title: First Entry
wildroots.journal.hint.welcome: New species: %s. Plants from one spot are not alike. Sow seed from the best, and the offspring seem to take after them.
wildroots.journal.species.wild_carrot.se: White umbels, visible from far off. A single dark purple floret often sits at the centre of each. The root is thin and white, smells of carrot, and can be bitter. Roots from one patch differ noticeably.
wildroots.journal.species.wild_carrot.hi: Wild carrot grows across Europe and western Asia; in North America it's called Queen Anne's lace. Its root is white and tough. It seems people first valued it not for the root but for its fragrant leaves and seeds.
wildroots.journal.cultivar.eastern_carro: A root that isn't bitter, at least medium, and a little sweet. And coloured: yellow or purple.
wildroots.journal.cultivar.carrot.goal: A very large, sweet root with no bitterness. And orange, without a trace of purple.
wildroots.cultivar.eastern_carrot.note: Coloured carrots, purple and yellow, arose in Central Asia and Afghanistan. By around the 10th century Persian writers describe them as a vegetable, and by the 12th they had reached Spain.
wildroots.cultivar.carrot.note: Orange carrots spread through Europe in the 16th–17th centuries, and Dutch growers made them the standard. The story that they were bred to honour the House of Orange has no evidence behind it. The colour is beta-carotene, which the body turns into vitamin A.
wildroots.journal.tool.field_journal: Everything found and bred is written here. A lost journal can be made again; the notes won't go anywhere.
wildroots.journal.tool.seed_pouch: A seed pouch. The packets inside never mix; each lies apart, and the last one put in is the first to come out.
wildroots.journal.hint.mother_plant: A pulled root can be eaten, or planted. Planted, it flowers and sets seed, and it's the same plant with all its merits. That's how selection goes: dig up, look, put the best back.
wildroots.journal.hint.plant_together: Plants of one kind pollinate each other when they grow close. A lone plant pollinates itself, which is said to bode ill.
wildroots.journal.hint.lone_plant.title: Alone in the Field
wildroots.journal.hint.lone_plant: This plant stands alone. If none of its kind flowers nearby, it will pollinate itself, and the offspring may come out weak.
wildroots.journal.hint.small_population: The bed is too small. A handful gives little to choose from, and rare traits slip away. A five-by-five bed is a good rule of thumb.
wildroots.journal.hint.select_quarter: Every fourth plant, the very best, is enough for seed. Choosier is faster, but it's easy to lose what hasn't shown itself yet.
wildroots.journal.hint.left_on_stalk: Left in the ground, the plant flowered on its own. Convenient, but nobody ever saw the root. Selection blindfolded.
wildroots.journal.hint.bitter.title: Bitter
wildroots.journal.hint.bitter: Bitter. But only some plants are, not all, which means the bitterness can be left behind next generation.
wildroots.journal.hint.yellow_root.title: A Yellow Root
wildroots.journal.hint.yellow_root: A yellow root! This may be how the eastern carrot began. The colour only shows when both parents pass it on; in the rest it can hide.
wildroots.journal.hint.orange_root.title: Orange
wildroots.journal.hint.orange_root: An orange root. Yellow alone isn't enough: it needs a second hidden trait, again from both parents. Guard it closely.
wildroots.journal.hint.purple_root.title: Purple
wildroots.journal.hint.purple_root: A purple root. This colour is strong: one parent is enough. But it masks both yellow and orange.
wildroots.journal.hint.bees.title: Bees
wildroots.journal.hint.bees: Bees hop from flower to flower, carrying pollen between plants. After their visits there's noticeably more seed.
wildroots.journal.hint.no_pollinators: Few seeds set. It seems nobody visited the flowers. Pollinators are needed; a wild bee nest nearby can be moved, if handled with a very gentle touch.
wildroots.journal.hint.inbreeding.title: Ailing
wildroots.journal.hint.inbreeding: Pale, short plants. Their parents were too closely related, or one plant pollinated itself. Fresh blood from another patch usually helps.
wildroots.journal.hint.hybrid_vigor: Two ailing lines gave sturdy offspring. Their weaknesses must have been different ones, and in the hybrid each covered for the other.
wildroots.journal.hint.stagnation.title: Stalled
wildroots.journal.hint.stagnation: Line %s has stalled: three generations without progress. The variety seems used up. Fresh stock is needed, from another biome, a village, a feral garden or an old cache. A plant breeder can tell where to look.
wildroots.journal.hint.missing_allele: Line %s seems to have no carriers of the trait it needs. The only way back is crossing with plants that have it.
wildroots.journal.hint.second_biome: Another patch, somewhere else, and these plants are strong in other ways. Brought together, they'll give more than either alone.
wildroots.journal.hint.climate.title: Out of Its Element
wildroots.journal.hint.climate: This plant is out of its climate: it grows, but grudgingly. Select the hardiest, or plant it somewhere more familiar.
wildroots.journal.hint.bone_meal.title: A Feed
wildroots.journal.hint.bone_meal: Bone meal hurries growth but doesn't improve the plant. The offspring won't change for it.
wildroots.journal.hint.unattended.title: Unattended
wildroots.journal.hint.unattended: Seed gathered unattended; who pollinated the flowers is anyone's guess. Best treat it as selfed.
wildroots.journal.hint.looks_like.title: Looks Like It, But…
wildroots.journal.hint.looks_like: This plant looks like %s. Looking like isn't being, though. Sow its seed and see whether the trait holds in the offspring.
wildroots.journal.hint.first_landrace: A landrace: a local variety. Not everything one could want, but no longer wild. Edible, not bitter, and its traits hold. The first farmers' gardens looked like this.
wildroots.journal.hint.first_cultivar: A cultivar. Every plant in it descends from that first one, where it all began.
wildroots.journal.hint.mutation.title: An Odd One
wildroots.journal.hint.mutation: An unusual plant that resembles neither parent. That's rare. Its seed is worth saving.
wildroots.journal.hint.carrier.title: Carrier
wildroots.journal.hint.carrier: The analyser found a carrier: the trait is there but hidden, invisible from outside. Cross two carriers and about a quarter of the offspring will show it.
wildroots.journal.hint.half_fixed.title: Not Yet Fixed
wildroots.journal.hint.half_fixed: The cultivar rests on one copy of the trait out of two. About a quarter of the offspring will lose it. To fix it, look for plants that got it from both parents.
wildroots.journal.hint.seed_pouch.title: The Pouch
wildroots.journal.hint.seed_pouch: Seed packets no longer spill across every pocket. In the pouch each lies apart, and the last one in is the first one out.
wildroots.message.journal.new_entry.body: Open the field journal to read it
item.wildroots.hand_lens.desc: Use on a plant, or with seeds in the other hand.
wildroots.journal.tool.hand_lens: The lens shows what the eye can't judge: taste, hardiness, how pollination went, whether a plant is ailing. Works on plants and on seed packets alike.
